newsitem.title: USA: US woman charged in Sandoz insider trading case.
newsitem.headline: US woman charged in Sandoz insider trading case.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday charged a former New York-based public relations senior account representative with violating federal securities laws related to an insider trading scheme.

In a civil complaint filed on Thursday in U.S. District Court in Savannah, Ga., the SEC alleged Susan Hirsch, a former employee of Ruder-Finn Inc, passed confidential information about a tender by a unit of Sandoz AG.

The complaint alleged Hirsch obtained information about Sandoz's confidential bid for GTI in advance of the July 1995 tender offer and tipped her brother Gregory Hirsch, a certified public accountant, the commission said.

SEC alleged Gregory Hirsch tipped and purchased GTI common stock and call options jointly with a friend in Savannah, Danny Kaminsky, in advance of the announcement for profits of $251,190, the commission said.

It further alleges on July 7, 1995, the last trading day before the tender, Kaminsky bought 45 GTI call options through a brokerage account of one of his friends, at a time when Kaminsky knew Sandoz was going to announce its offer for GTI at $21 per share the following Monday.
GTI is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sandoz.

Attorneys for Susan Hirsch have not seen the complaint and will have "no comment until we have the opportunity to review it", said Maureen Weiss, of Morgan, Lewis and Bockius LLP., in New York, one of the attorneys representing Hirsch.
Hirsch worked for Ruder-Finn in New York City from about the spring of 1992 to March 1996. She currently resides in Italy, but her permanent address is Savannah, Ga.
Kaminsky is co-owner of Southern Motors, an automobile dealership in Savannah, Ga.

Also named in the civil complaint is Lewis Kooden, a vice president of ALKO Distributors Inc, a beer and wine distributorship; Daniel Klugman, a general manager of ALKO and Lewis Kooden's nephew and Michael Kooden, Lewis Kooden's son and ALKO, the commission said.
In December 1996, the U.S. federal government conditionally approved the merger of Swiss drug giants Ciba-Geigy Ag and Sandoz Ag to create Novartis.
